name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_Q01 - Five-statement evaluation of the four basic animal tissues

questiontext.text:
Consider the following five statements regarding animal tissues:

Statement I: Squamous epithelium is found in the walls of blood vessels and air sacs of lungs where it forms a diffusion boundary.

Statement II: Exocrine glands secrete mucus, saliva, earwax, oil, milk, and digestive enzymes through ducts or tubes.

Statement III: Connective tissues are the most abundant and widely distributed tissues in the body of complex animals.

Statement IV: Cardiac muscle tissue is present in the heart as well as in the walls of the stomach and intestine.

Statement V: Neuroglia protect and support neurons and make up more than one-half the volume of neural tissue in the body.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Complex animals are built from four basic tissue types—epithelial, connective, muscular, and neural—each with distinct locations and physiological roles.

Step 2: Evaluation of Epithelial and Glandular Claims
Simple squamous epithelium forms a thin layer in blood vessel walls and lung air sacs to facilitate diffusion. Exocrine glands release secretions such as mucus, saliva, earwax, oil, milk, and digestive enzymes via ducts. Both claims are correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Connective and Neural Claims
Connective tissues are indeed the most abundant and widely distributed tissues in complex animals. In neural tissue, neuroglial cells protect and support excitable neurons and constitute more than half of the total neural tissue volume. Both claims are correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of Cardiac Muscle Location
Cardiac muscle tissue is a contractile tissue present exclusively in the heart; the walls of internal organs such as the stomach, intestine, and blood vessels contain smooth muscle tissue instead. Therefore, placing cardiac muscle in the stomach and intestine is incorrect.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The claims regarding squamous epithelium, exocrine glands, connective tissue abundance, and neuroglial volume are correct, while the claim placing cardiac muscle in the stomach and intestine is incorrect.

answer.text: Statements I, II, III and IV only
Statements I, II, III and V only
Statements I, III, IV and V only
All Statements I, II, III, IV and V

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_Q02 - Five-statement evaluation of earthworm morphology, nephridia and reproduction

questiontext.text:
Read the following five statements regarding the earthworm (*Pheretima*):

Statement I: The cylindrical body is divided into about 100–120 similar short segments called metameres.

Statement II: The dorsal surface is marked by a dark median mid-dorsal line representing the dorsal blood vessel.

Statement III: The epidermis of the body wall consists of a single layer of columnar epithelial cells containing secretory gland cells.

Statement IV: Integumentary nephridia are attached to the lining of the body wall from segment 3 to the last and open into the intestine.

Statement V: Earthworms are protandrous animals, and each cocoon produces an average of four baby worms after about 3 weeks.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Earthworms exhibit metameric segmentation, a glandular columnar epidermis, three regionally specialised nephridial types, and protandrous hermaphroditic reproduction via cocoons.

Step 2: Evaluation of Segmentation, Dorsal Line and Epidermis
The body consists of roughly 100–120 similar metameres, bears a dark median mid-dorsal line corresponding to the dorsal blood vessel, and has an epidermis made of a single layer of columnar epithelial cells with secretory gland cells beneath a thin cuticle. All three claims are correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Integumentary Nephridia
Integumentary nephridia are attached to the body wall lining from segment 3 to the last segment, but they open externally on the body surface (exonephric), whereas septal nephridia open into the intestine. Thus, claiming that integumentary nephridia open into the intestine is incorrect.

Step 4: Evaluation of Reproduction and Cocoon Development
Earthworms are protandrous with cross-fertilisation, and each cocoon deposited in soil produces two to twenty baby worms with an average of four after about 3 weeks. This claim is correct.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The claims regarding metameres, the dorsal blood vessel line, columnar epidermis, and protandrous cocoon development are correct, while the claim that integumentary nephridia open into the intestine is incorrect.

answer.text: Statements I, II, III and IV only
Statements I, III, IV and V only
Statements II, III, IV and V only
Statements I, II, III and V only

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_Q03 - Five-statement evaluation of cockroach morphology, excretion and moulting

questiontext.text:
Evaluate the following five statements regarding *Periplaneta americana*:

Statement I: Adults are about 34–53 mm long with wings that extend beyond the tip of the abdomen in males.

Statement II: Each of the three thoracic segments (prothorax, mesothorax, and metathorax) bears a pair of walking legs.

Statement III: The entire foregut of the alimentary canal is lined internally by cuticle.

Statement IV: In addition to Malpighian tubules, the fat body, nephrocytes, and urecose glands also help in excretion.

Statement V: The nymph grows by moulting about 5 times to reach the adult form.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Cockroaches possess characteristic body dimensions, three pairs of thoracic walking legs, a cuticle-lined foregut, accessory excretory structures, and gradual nymphal development.

Step 2: Evaluation of Size, Legs and Foregut Lining
Adult *Periplaneta americana* measure 34–53 mm in length with wings extending beyond the abdominal tip in males. Each of the three thoracic segments bears one pair of walking legs, and the entire foregut is lined by cuticle. All three claims are correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Accessory Excretory Structures
While Malpighian tubules perform the main excretory function, the fat body, nephrocytes, and urecose glands also assist in excretion. This claim is correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of Nymphal Moulting
In paurometabolous development, the nymph grows by moulting about 13 times (not 5 times) to reach the adult form, with wing pads appearing in the next-to-last nymphal stage. Thus, stating that the nymph moults about 5 times is incorrect.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The first four claims regarding adult size, thoracic walking legs, foregut cuticle lining, and accessory excretory structures are correct, whereas the claim regarding the number of nymphal moults is incorrect.

answer.text: Statements I, II, III and IV only
Statements I, II, III and V only
Statements II, III, IV and V only
All Statements I, II, III, IV and V

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_Q04 - Five-statement evaluation of frog respiration, blood, brain and reproduction

questiontext.text:
Consider the following five statements regarding the Indian bullfrog (*Rana tigrina*):

Statement I: On land, the buccal cavity, skin, and lungs act as the respiratory organs.

Statement II: Red blood cells (RBCs) are nucleated and contain haemoglobin, whereas lymph lacks few proteins and RBCs.

Statement III: The mid-brain is characterised by a pair of optic lobes, and the hind-brain consists of the cerebellum and medulla oblongata.

Statement IV: In male frogs, the ureters act as urinogenital ducts opening into the cloaca, whereas in females the ureters and oviducts open separately into the cloaca.

Statement V: A mature female lays about 250 to 300 ova at a time, and fertilisation is internal.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Frogs exhibit terrestrial and aquatic respiratory adaptations, nucleated erythrocytes, a tripartite vertebrate brain, sex-specific urinogenital openings, and external aquatic fertilisation.

Step 2: Evaluation of Respiration, Blood and Brain
On land, frogs respire using the buccal cavity, skin, and lungs. Their RBCs are nucleated and contain haemoglobin, while lymph differs from blood by lacking RBCs and a few proteins. The mid-brain features a pair of optic lobes, and the hind-brain comprises the cerebellum and medulla oblongata. All three claims are correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Urinogenital Ducts
In male frogs, the two ureters emerging from the kidneys function as urinogenital ducts carrying both urine and sperms to the cloaca, whereas in female frogs the ureters and oviducts open separately into the cloaca. This claim is correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of Oviposition and Fertilisation
A mature female frog lays 2500 to 3000 ova at a time (not 250 to 300), and fertilisation is external in water (not internal). Thus, this claim is incorrect.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The first four claims describing terrestrial respiration, blood/lymph composition, brain divisions, and sex-specific cloacal ducts are correct, while the claim regarding egg count and internal fertilisation is incorrect.

Statements I, III, IV and V only
Statements I, II, III and IV only
All Statements I, II, III, IV and V

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_Q05 - Five-statement comparative synthesis across tissues, earthworm, cockroach and frog

questiontext.text:
Read the following five statements across animal organisation:

Statement I: Cells, tissues, organs, and organ systems split up work in multicellular animals to exhibit division of labour.

Statement II: In earthworms, the alimentary canal is a straight tube running from the first to the last segment, with the stomach extending from segments 9–14.

Statement III: In cockroaches, the hindgut is broader than the midgut and is differentiated into ileum, colon, and rectum.

Statement IV: In frogs, the urinary bladder is thick-walled, lies dorsal to the rectum, and does not open into the cloaca.

Statement V: In dense regular connective tissue, collagen fibres are present in rows between many parallel bundles of fibres, as seen in tendons and ligaments.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Multicellular animals exhibit division of labour across hierarchical levels of organisation, with distinct anatomical arrangements in annelids, arthropods, and amphibians.

Step 2: Evaluation of Division of Labour and Connective Tissue
Cells, tissues, organs, and organ systems divide physiological tasks to ensure survival of the whole body. In dense regular connective tissues such as tendons and ligaments, collagen fibres lie in rows between parallel fibre bundles. Both claims are correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Earthworm and Cockroach Alimentary Canals
The earthworm alimentary canal is a straight tube from the first to the last segment with the stomach spanning segments 9–14. In cockroaches, the hindgut is broader than the midgut and is differentiated into ileum, colon, and rectum. Both claims are correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of Frog Urinary Bladder
In frogs, the urinary bladder is thin-walled (not thick-walled), lies ventral (not dorsal) to the rectum, and opens into the cloaca. Therefore, the description of the frog's urinary bladder is incorrect.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The claims regarding division of labour, earthworm alimentary canal, cockroach hindgut, and dense regular connective tissue are correct, whereas the claim describing the frog's urinary bladder is incorrect.
